summary: Hocking County steel fire tower built in summer 1929 at Rock House, a 65-foot tower; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site

events.note: Built in summer 1929, per a December 1929 Athens Messenger item
Fire guard near the tower saw smoke south of the cave; rangers fought a fire in a hollow some miles away

evidence.supports: built summer 1929; visitors climbed the observation room
evidence.quote: Since the fire tower was constructed at the Rockhouse this summer hundreds of visitors have climbed to the observation room at its top to view the surrounding territory.

evidence.supports: one of three new 65-foot steel towers, one on Rock House State Park
evidence.quote: Ohio has three new 65-foot steel fire towers ready for operation--one on Rock House State Park, Hocking County.

evidence.supports: register places the site in Hocking State Forest
May 1931 fire guard saw smoke from south of the cave
evidence.quote: Luther Carr, fire guard, was roofing a building near the fire tower when he detected smoke coming from south of the cave.

evidence.supports: fire placed in a hollow some miles away
evidence.quote: A survey placed the fire in a hollow some miles away.

evidence.supports: rangers raked a path through the leaves and set a backfire
evidence.quote: rangers commenced raking a path through the leaves where they started a back fire.

evidence.supports: October 1934 Ira Oldfield selected as towerman
evidence.quote: At Rock House, Ira Oldfield has been selected towerman.

evidence.supports: agency is the Ohio Department of Natural Resources
Ohio list marks the tower as gone
evidence.quote: Rock House Hocking 39.49548 -82.61247 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1570, OH 16

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts entry ends with the word Removed, no date given

notes_for_editor: Built date is inferred from the December 1929 item, which says the tower was constructed this summer. The record's 19.8 m matches the 65-foot figure. Removal date and method are unknown; the Forest Lookouts page gives only the word Removed. The 1930 item says Rock House State Park and the register says Hocking State Forest; not reconciled. Two search snippets (not read, not used) describe a Rock House Lookout Tower at the end of a Hocking Hills gorge trail and a TopoQuest map feature with that name. Both conflict with gone and should be checked before any claim about the site today.
